2. `/dashboard/dedicated/order/[id]`: Configure — location (only in-stock locations selectable), memory, storage (combinations not in stock are disabled; picking one auto-switches the other to an in-stock partner), network (bandwidth options, when more than one exists), OS (`lib/dedicated/order-core.ts` `DEDICATED_OS`: Ubuntu 24.04/22.04, Debian 12, AlmaLinux 9, Rocky 9, Proxmox VE 8; installed by staff), term (Monthly, or Annual = 12 x monthly up front, no discount because the pricing rules define none), optional name. Every price on this step comes from a server-computed price table (`loadOrderBuild`), the same function the charge uses.
3. Review — the server re-quotes (`quoteDedicatedOrderAction`): specs, location, OS, term, setup, tax (destination VAT via `taxContextForUser`, same as VPS), total today, renewal stated as charged (`$X/mo` or `$X/yr`), wallet toggle with the split.
4. Pay — the portal's standard wallet-then-card path: wallet covers it -> placed immediately; otherwise a Stripe Custom Checkout session (`createDedicatedOrderPaymentSession`, ui_mode `elements`, rendered inline by `components/nx/NxCardFields`) for exactly the card remainder. Metadata `nxeonDedicatedOrder` (intent) + `nxeonDedicatedOrderPrice` (stamped price). `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` (`dedicatedOrder` branch) credits the card leg to the wallet, then `placeDedicatedOrder` debits the STAMPED total. Card-leg sessions are purchase legs (`isPurchaseLegSession`), so no duplicate top-up invoice. PayPal/crypto/local methods are not offered for dedicated orders yet.
5. The order lands as a `DedicatedServer` with status **PENDING**: frozen specs, region, OS label, `renewalMonthlyCents` + `termMonths`, renewal date (order date + term), setup fee, the PAID invoice id, and admin-only fields (`datacenter` with the best stock at order time, `costMonthlyCents`, `notes`, `orderConfig` JSON with the upstream plan/option codes). The customer gets an in-app notification; every ADMIN gets one linking to `/admin/dedicated/servers/<id>`, whose new "Online order — build this by hand" panel shows the full build sheet.
6. Customer dashboard `/dashboard/dedicated/[id]`: status timeline (Order received -> Being built -> Online), specs, IPs once assigned, login reveal, renewal ("$X/yr" for annual), invoices, support, request buttons once ACTIVE. `?ordered=1` shows the confirmation banner.

**Money safety.** One order key per checkout (client-generated) is claimed in `FulfilledSession` as `dedorder:<userId>:<key>`, so a double click, a retry, or the webhook/redirect race places at most one order and debits once. Wallet debit, wallet transaction, PAID invoice, server row, event and audit log are one transaction (spend caps honoured). A failed wallet placement releases the claim. A card-leg failure after capture is recorded FAILED and the customer is told the money is in their wallet (`notifyStalled`). Impersonating admins cannot pay. Unverified emails cannot pay (`emailVerificationError`).

**Not built (owner decisions).** Automatic renewal charging for dedicated servers (renewals stay manual, as before); partner/creator commission on dedicated invoices; PayPal/crypto for dedicated; an annual discount; cancellation/refund flow (staff, by hand).

**Schema (additive):** `DedicatedServer.orderKey String?` (indexed) and `DedicatedServer.orderConfig Json?`.

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

content.thinking:
Checking the OVH dedicated server API, the reboot endpoint only supports a hard reboot/power cycle—there's no true soft reboot option since that would require OS-level access we don't have. So I should only expose "Hard reboot (power cycle)" as an action and note this limitation in the report.

For rescue mode, I'm looking at GET /dedicated/server/{sn}/boot?bootType=rescue to find the rescue boot id, then PUT /dedicated/server/{sn} with that bootId plus a reboot call. Rather than relying on OVH emailing a password, I can use the rescueSshKey field so the customer's own SSH key grants rescue access with no password needed—though if OVH still emails credentials in some cases, I'll let staff store those encrypted for reveal using the same pattern as the existing credentialsEnc column, just under a new rescueCredEnc field.

For reinstalling, I'm weighing the older POST /dedicated/server/{sn}/install/start approach against the newer /reinstall endpoint OVH introduced, since the legacy one is being deprecated — I'll go with POST /dedicated/server/{sn}/reinstall passing operatingSystem and customizations (hostname, sshKey), pulling compatible templates from GET /dedicated/server/{sn}/install/compatibleTemplates, and tracking install progress through the status/task polling endpoint.

For remote console access, requesting KVM/IPMI access returns a URL that's an OVH-hosted proxy page rather than something directly embeddable for customers, and the serial-over-LAN option is similarly tied to an OVH host — so I'm noting in my report that this can't be shipped to customers directly and should instead surface as "ask support" rather than building a worker path around it.

For extra IP ordering, the real flow is more involved: customer purchase goes through checkout, creates a DedicatedIpOrder row pending approval, admin approves, then a worker job builds the OVH cart (assigning it, adding the IP product with plan code, duration, and configuration like country/destination). Since this involves real spend via the OVH API, I'm planning to implement the job with a dry-run mode that constructs the cart steps without executing real purchases.

I should check for existing monthly cent pricing for dedicated IPs. Given the scope here, I need to prioritize sensibly while reporting honestly — tokens aren't the constraint, but quality is, so I'll structure Phase 2 around building a dedicated ops planner module with an injectable client for operation planning.

I'm sketching out the plan functions: reboot, rescue mode (boot into rescue, optionally with an SSH key, then reboot), and disk boot mode, each following a get-boot-id then put-then-reboot pattern. Then I'm working out how to list installation templates — fetching compatible templates and their descriptions, then mapping OVH's internal names to clean customer-facing labels by stripping the "ovh" prefix and filtering down to known OS families like Ubuntu, Debian, Alma, Rocky, and Proxmox.

Now I'm mapping out reinstall via POST to the server's reinstall endpoint, reverse DNS management (noting that lib/ovh-admin/reverse.ts already handles this, so I should reuse it), and firewall rules — both reusing existing game firewall actions and handling customer network firewall rules through the IP block's firewall endpoint. I'm also cataloging the read-only endpoints needed for status, hardware specs, and bandwidth info.

For traffic quotas, I can reuse the existing parseNetworkSpec and trafficVerdict helpers along with parseServer, and parseTask already covers polling task status. On the worker side, I'm planning dedicated-jobs.ts to atomically claim QUEUED jobs via updateMany, then execute them either with real audited OVH writes (actor set to the customer id) or in DRY-RUN mode, defaulting the dedicated_ovh_dry_run setting to "true" for safety.

In dry-run mode, writes get logged but never sent, and the job completes marked "(dry run)" until the owner flips it live; I'm also adding a hard safety guard that refuses any write if the target service name matches a Node's providerServerId, so a typo can never accidentally reboot a Proxmox node. For the demo, I'll seed a mock DedicatedServer row with a fake providerServiceName and use the NXEON_OVH_ADMIN_STUB env flag so the dev stub serves fake GETs, which means extending the shared stub.ts to handle dedicated server endpoints too.

I'm leaning toward building a self-contained fixture-based mock client at lib/dedicated/ovh-mock.ts gated by its own mock flag, rather than overloading the shared stub. For the customer-facing web tier, I'll allow read-only GETs for hardware/status but cache them via a server action with a short in-memory TTL to avoid hammering OVH on every page load. For ordering extra IPs, I'm weighing whether to add a new Stripe purpose kind versus just reusing the existing wallet-then-card checkout flow to keep the surface area smaller.

Now I'm working out the pricing for extra IP purchases, pulling the monthly rate from the existing dedicated IP setting and multiplying by quantity, then figuring out whether to charge a full month or prorate to the server's renewal date like the dedicated-IP flow does—checking how that existing purchase path computes remaining-term proration so I can mirror it here.

On approval, the renewal amount gets bumped by the monthly rate times quantity. I'm sketching a new DedicatedIpOrder model to track the request lifecycle—paid, approved, ordering, done, rejected, failed—plus an admin UI on the server detail page to approve or reject (with wallet refund on rejection), where approval kicks off a DedicatedJob to actually order the IP. I also want to support both wallet and card payments by adding a "dedicatedAddon" classifier kind.

After the IP is delivered and the admin flags it, I'll trigger an auto-install job using the chosen OS, the customer's SSH keys, and hostname, marking the resource ACTIVE and notifying the customer via the templated email system once done—though I need to make sure no real emails fire during testing since my dev environment lacks SMTP credentials. For root password delivery after reinstall, SSH-key-based installs skip passwords entirely, so I'm weighing whether to require an SSH key or rely on OVH emailing the account owner directly.

If a customer has no SSH key, the UI should prompt them to add one in settings, so I'm checking how the SshKey model stores and manages keys. This is a large task, so I'm breaking it into pieces — first reviewing the SshKey model, the email template system, the OVH admin reverse/parse helpers, the dedicated endpoint stubs, and the network firewall write actions.

content.thinking:
I'm sketching the schema for a new DedicatedJob model, linking it to the DedicatedServer table via a relation field, and adding a userId column.

I'm also incrementing renewal cost on DONE. I'm designing the pure ops executor in lib/dedicated/ops.ts, with a step function run repeatedly by the worker until each job reaches a terminal state, like REINSTALL moving from start to posting the reinstall request to polling task completion. I'm wrapping writes in an audited function that records actor identity and supports dry-run mode, plus adding safety guards like ensuring service names are validated against known server identifiers.

I need to confirm the server status requirements and IP validation checks for actions like rDNS and firewall changes, then set up the sweep worker to claim jobs every 10 seconds, distinguish mock versus real dependencies, respect a dry-run flag, and time out stale WAITING jobs after 2 hours. I'm now worried that having dry-run on by default means a real customer could trigger an action and see it marked "done" without anything actually happening on the OVH side.

For the preview, dry-run is safe since the job should finish as DONE but surface a visible "dry run" note to the user. For customer actions, I want to confirm each is gated behind ownership, active status, rate limiting, and an impersonation check, with reinstall requiring the user to type the server's name as confirmation, and reads being allowed against real OVH (or fixtures in mock mode) even though writes go through the job queue instead.

The mock server data needs a fake service name since reads must pull from mock when NXEON_DEDICATED_OVH_MOCK=1 is set in non-prod, and actions should only ever accept our internal serverId, never a raw service name from the customer. For the templates mapping, I'm defining regex patterns to translate OVH's compatible template names into friendly customer labels—matching Ubuntu, Debian, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, Proxmox VE, and Fedora versions while skipping CentOS and unknown/Windows templates.

Customers select templates by name, validated against the compatible list both in the worker and the action, and while raw names appear as values, the UI should only display the friendly labels. For reinstall, I'll use the newer OVH endpoint with operatingSystem and customizations fields for hostname and SSH key, documenting that this is per the v1 API spec but only verified against fixtures. For rescue mode, I'm using a PUT to update bootId and rescueSshKey followed by a reboot call—noting that if the customer has no SSH key, OVH falls back to emailing a rescue password to the account contact.

For the password handoff, staff will need to paste it into a stored field so customers can reveal it via decryption, so I'm planning admin storage plus customer reveal functionality. For firewall management, I'm reusing existing parsing and request-building helpers to let customers list, add, remove, and toggle rules, while skipping game firewall support since it's irrelevant for dedicated servers. For hardware, status, and bandwidth, I'll pull server details, specs, and boot info to surface power state, boot mode, traffic quotas, and link speed. Console access isn't shipped, so I'll just note it's available but unsupported in this interface.

For extra IPs, I'm figuring out a purchase flow offering quantities like 1, 2, 4, or 8 (mapping to IP block sizes), with prorated pricing based on remaining days until renewal, and reusing the existing dedicated order mechanism with new metadata rather than building a separate billing path to keep scope minimal.

Now I'm sketching the admin approval UI for dedicated servers, letting staff approve (which enqueues an IP order job) or reject (refunding the wallet). For the job executor itself, I'm working out the OVH cart API sequence — creating a cart, assigning it, then querying service options to find the right plan code matching the requested IP block size, though I'm still unsure of the exact plan code naming.

I need to map plan codes like "ip-v4-sXX-ripe" to block sizes using the subnet suffix, then add the chosen option to the cart with the right quantity, and finally attach required configuration items like country and destination to the cart item.

Once configuration is set, I'll checkout the cart with auto-pay and retractation waiver to get an orderId, then poll the order status until it's delivered, and compare the server's IP list before/after to identify and attach the newly assigned IPs.

For dry-run mode, I'll record each planned API call without actually executing any writes beyond cart creation (which is harmless), just reporting the plan; with a mock client, I can run the full flow against fixtures and write unit tests verifying the exact call sequence per job type and guard condition.

For the handover feature, I'm designing an admin "Deliver & auto-install" button that requires a providerServiceName to be set, which enqueues a HANDOVER job once delivery completes.

For reinstall, I need to map our internal OS id to the matching OVH template by family/version, and pass the customer's SSH key — using the first key if they have multiple, but if they have none the job should fail with a clear admin message since there's no good fallback (OVH could email root credentials, but manual delivery via the existing CredentialsForm is simpler). On DONE, I'll set status to ACTIVE, record provisionedAt, backfill ipv4 from the server's IP endpoint if missing, and trigger notifications/emails through the existing template system — I should check how sendTemplate is used elsewhere.

/// One automated action on a delivered dedicated server (Phase 2). The web tier

model DedicatedJob {

  server            DedicatedServer @relation(fields: [dedicatedServerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  /// Who asked (customer or staff).

  /// QUEUED | RUNNING | WAITING | DONE | FAILED
  status            String          @default("QUEUED")
  payload           Json
  /// Executor-private state between ticks (phase, upstream task/order ids).
  state             Json?
  step              String          @default("Queued")
  progress          Int             @default(0)
  dryRun            Boolean         @default(false)
  error             String?
  attempts          Int             @default(0)
  createdAt         DateTime        @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime        @updatedAt
  startedAt         DateTime?
  finishedAt        DateTime?

  @@index([status, updatedAt])
  @@index([dedicatedServerId, createdAt])
}

/// upstream (IP_ORDER job). Rejecting refunds the charge to the wallet.
model DedicatedIpOrder {
  id                String          @id @default(cuid())
  dedicatedServerId String
  server            DedicatedServer @relation(fields: [dedicatedServerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  userId            String
  quantity          Int
  /// Nxeon monthly price per IP at purchase time.
  unitMonthlyCents  Int
  /// What the customer paid now (prorated to the next renewal).
  chargedCents      Int
  invoiceId         String?
  orderKey          String
  /// PAID | APPROVED | ORDERING | DONE | REJECTED | FAILED
  status            String          @default("PAID")
  approvedById      String?
  approvedAt        DateTime?
  rejectReason      String?
  jobId             String?
  ips               String[]        @default([])
  createdAt         DateTime        @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime        @updatedAt

  @@index([status, createdAt])
  @@index([dedicatedServerId])
  @@index([orderKey])
}
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

I'm sketching the pure executor in lib/dedicated/ops.ts, defining an OpsClient interface with get and write methods that handle requests with action, method, path, body, target, and noop/read flags, returning typed success or error results.

Now I'm defining the job and server context types (JobRow, ServerCtx) plus a StepResult type capturing status, step, progress, errors, and side effects like server patches, IP order patches, or handover notifications, and sketching runJobStep's signature that takes a job, server, and dependencies and returns a StepResult.

I'm adding guard checks at the top for required and non-protected service names plus kind-specific status validation, then working through the job kind logic: REBOOT_HARD triggers a reboot task and polls until done or failed, RESCUE_ON fetches the rescue boot type, sets the boot config, reboots, and polls, and RESCUE_OFF mirrors that flow using the hard disk boot type.

For REINSTALL and HANDOVER, I'm validating the template against the compatible list, triggering the reinstall API with hostname and SSH key customizations, and polling the install status endpoint for progress with a fallback to task status, applying handover effects like marking the server active and backfilling IPs when the install completes. For REVERSE_SET, I'm working out how to determine the correct IP block (main IP as /32 versus subnet blocks for additional IPs) so I can validate the target IP belongs to the server before setting the reverse DNS.

I can derive the block by matching the IP against the CIDR list from the server's IP endpoint, then issue the reverse DNS update, which completes immediately. For firewall actions, I'm handling enabling/disabling by creating the firewall entry if missing then toggling it, and for rule management I'm adding or removing specific firewall rules by sequence number.

For dry runs, since there's no real cart to progress through, I'll handle IP_ORDER specially by just planning the steps and marking it done without any real effects. For other write operations, I think the simplest approach is to have the executor check the dryRun flag and short-circuit to DONE right after the first write phase, skipping polling entirely.

For mock mode though, I want the full flow to run against a stateful in-memory fake OVH that simulates tasks completing after a couple of polls, so the demo actually shows progress. The real worker dependencies wire up admin OVH get/write functions, with the write path carrying actor info and a dangerous rate class for risky actions like reboot, rescue, and reinstall.

The tricky part is that ovhAdminWrite needs a read function, and since the web tier and worker run as separate processes, an in-memory mock state wouldn't be shared between them -- so for the demo I'd need to either run the actual worker or write a small script that loops the dedicated-jobs tick function directly with the mock client, and figure out how to persist mock state across that gap.

I'm settling on persisting mock state to a JSON file in the temp directory (dev-only, controlled by an env var with a default path), so both web reads and worker writes stay consistent for things like power and boot mode. Now I'm sketching out the web-tier read service that would pull live server status -- power, state, boot mode, hardware specs, and network info -- from that shared mock state.

I'm defining a templates list function and then a customer actions module with functions for loading live status and templates, plus an enqueue function that validates inputs per operation kind and enforces one in-flight job per server.

I'm adding rate limits (10/hour general, 4/hour for dangerous actions), typed confirmation matching the server name for reinstalls, SSH key selection, hostname validation reusing the FQDN rules but allowing single labels, plus job polling, rescue secret reveal, and IP purchase quoting/payment flows.

For admin operations I'm defining order approval/rejection with refunds, handover initiation that checks the server isn't protected, and rescue secret storage. I'm also mapping OS identifiers to compatible templates for handovers, falling back to admin intervention if no match exists, before moving into the worker implementation for dedicated server jobs.

The worker tick claims queued or stalled jobs, loads the server, builds dependencies, runs job steps, persists state, and notifies the customer in-app plus via email for handover completion — with a three-hour timeout marking stalled jobs as failed. I'm also setting up a dry-run flag that defaults to true unless running in mock mode, and defining protected service names from existing node providers plus an extra settings-based list, requiring the server's provider service name to match something in the actual OVH account.

Now I'm splitting the module into a pure, customer-safe core file for template labels, job kind labels, and validation, and a separate executor file that handles the actual server-side operations with injected dependencies.

55 tools/nxm/README.md
# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)
- Author in the package's own format under `tools/nxm/native/<slug>/`: `body.html` (with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}`), `page.css`, `page.js`, `meta.json` (`title`, `description`, `anchors`, `assets`). `port_pages.py` assembles them exactly like the package's `build_page.py` (shared shell + common.css + Aurora + your css/js) and runs the same pipeline. Add the slug to `ROUTES` in `nxmlib.py` (or a fan-out in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`).
- Reference implementations: `native/about` (story + liquid-glass photo + real product prices), `native/security` (diagram + card grids + the Compare page's disclosure board), `native/affiliate` (data-driven promo), `native/legal` (article reading layout, 4 routes from one template).
- Write markup with the DESIGN's classes (`au-btn`, `au-btn--glass`, `au-card`, `au-glass`, `h2pill`, `gp-head`, `h2`, `lede`, `section`, `container`, `faq-wrap`/`faq`, `wh-final`, `data-au-icon="…" data-grad`) — the porter maps buttons to the library hierarchy. Links to other pages as `https://nxeon.cloud/<route>` (the porter makes them relative / keeps ported ones inside /nxm).
- Pure-copy pages: a wire module with `STATIC = True` and no loader.
- Body attributes: `<body class="pg-x" style="--acc:…" data-…>` land on the page wrapper; `.pg-x …` selectors are rewritten to match it.
- Loader extras: `trail` (breadcrumb below Home when ancestors aren't in the registry), `particles` (per-item colours), `crumb`.
- Interactive React pieces (e.g. a live tool component) can be mounted into a slot element with a small client component + `createPortal` — see `app/nxm/_components/HeroParticles.tsx`.
- SEO for new routes: add an entry to `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (title/description/crumb) or return them from `meta(p)`.
- The box is also production: keep Playwright runs sequential (one browser at a time) and don't restart the shared dev server (:3033, 4 GB heap cap).

def load_wire(slug):
    f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/wire/{slug.replace('-', '_')}.py"
    if not os.path.exists(f):
        return None
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(f"wire_{slug}", f)
    m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    return m

PRICE = re.compile(r"\$\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d\d)?")
NUMPRICE = re.compile(r"""["']?\b(?:p|i|r|pr|price|priceUsd|from)["']?\s*:\s*\d+\.\d\d\b""")
def audit(slug, body, js, allow):
    """Every $-amount left in a page must be allowed (not ours). Returns the
    stale ones; a page with any is not launch-ready."""
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", body) + " " + js
    found = {m.group(0) for m in PRICE.finditer(text)}
    # prices held as bare numbers in data constants / JSON (p: 12.78, "price":4.99)
    found |= {m.group(0) for m in NUMPRICE.finditer(text)}
    return sorted(found - set(allow))

def js_buttons(js):
# ── native pages: pages the design package doesn't include ─────────────────
# Authored in the package's own page format (body.html with {{SPRITE}}/{{NAV}}/
# {{FOOTER}}, page.css, page.js, meta.json) under tools/nxm/native/<slug>/ and
# assembled exactly like the package's build_page.py: shared shell + common.css
# + aurora + the page's own css/js. Then the same pipeline as every page.
NATIVE = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/native"
def build_native(slug):
    D = f"{NATIVE}/{slug}/"
    meta = json.load(open(D + "meta.json"))
    p1, p2, p3 = (open(f"{SRC}/part{i}.html").read() for i in (1, 2, 3))
    MAIN = "https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs"
    head = re.sub(r"<title>.*?</title>", f"<title>{meta['title']}</title>", p1, count=1)
    head = re.sub(r'<meta name="description" content="[^"]*">', f'<meta name="description" content="{meta["description"]}">', head, count=1)
    head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', "none").replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', "none")
    css = open(f"{SRC}/pages/common.css").read() + AURORA_CSS + (open(D + "page.css").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.css") else "")
    head = head.replace("</style>", css + "</style>", 1)
    sprite = p2[p2.index("<body>") + 6:p2.index("</svg>") + 6]
    local = set(meta.get("anchors", []))
    def fix_links(h):
        h = re.sub(r'href="#([a-z-]*)"', lambda m: f'href="#{m.group(1)}"' if (m.group(1) in local or m.group(1).startswith("i-")) else f'href="{MAIN}#{m.group(1)}"', h)
        return h.replace(f'href="{MAIN}#top"', f'href="{MAIN}"')
    nav = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<a class="skip"'):p2.index("</header>") + 9]).replace(f'href="{MAIN}#main"', 'href="#main"')
    nav = nav.replace('<a class="logo" href="#top"', f'<a class="logo" href="{MAIN}"')
    footer = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<footer class="footer"'):p2.index("</footer>") + 9])
    body = open(D + "body.html").read()
    for k, v in {"SPRITE": sprite, "NAV": nav, "FOOTER": footer, "MAIN": MAIN}.items():
        body = body.replace("{{" + k + "}}", v)
    helpers = p3[p3.index("<script>"):p3.index("/* ------------------------------------------------------------------")]
    def blk(a, b): i = p3.index(a); j = p3.index(b, i + len(a)); return p3[i:j]
    js = helpers + "document.getElementById('year') && (document.getElementById('year').textContent = new Date().getFullYear());\n"
    js += blk("/* ============ Navigation ============ */", "/* ============ Reveal, rules")
    js += blk("/* ============ Reveal, rules, in-view hooks, counters ============ */", "/* ============ Hero: Power Your")
    js += AURORA_JS + "\n" + (open(D + "page.js").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.js") else "") + "\n})();\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n"
    html = head + body + js
    A = f"{PKG}/assets/"
    m = {k: (v if v.startswith("/") else A + v) for k, v in meta.get("assets", {}).items()}
    m.setdefault("LOGO", A + "logo.png")
    for _k in ["minecraft", "rust", "palworld", "valheim", "ark", "cs2"]:
        m.setdefault("NAV_" + _k.upper(), A + "nav/" + _k + ".webp")
    mime = lambda q: "image/png" if q.endswith(".png") else "image/svg+xml" if q.endswith(".svg") else "image/jpeg" if q.endswith(".jpg") else "image/webp"
    for k in sorted(m, key=len, reverse=True):
        html = html.replace(f"__IMG_{k}__", f"data:{mime(m[k])};base64," + _fake_b64(open(m[k], "rb").read()).decode())
    left = set(re.findall(r"__IMG_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__", html)); assert not left, left
    return html

EXT = {"image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp", "image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/svg+xml": "svg", "image/gif": "gif"}
def externalise(s):
def port(slug):
    html = externalise(build_native(slug) if os.path.isdir(f"{NATIVE}/{slug}") else build(slug))
    head, rest = html.split("</head>", 1)
    title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", head).group(1)
    desc_m = re.search(r'<meta name="description" content="([^"]*)"', head)
    desc = desc_m.group(1) if desc_m else ""

    # CSS: the page's one stylesheet minus Aurora (already loaded, scoped, by
    # app/nxm/layout.tsx), scoped under this page's wrapper.
    css = re.search(r"<style>([\s\S]*)</style>", head).group(1)
    assert AURORA_CSS in css, "aurora.css not found verbatim"
    css = geist(css.replace(AURORA_CSS, ""))
    scope, rootcls = f".nxm-p-{slug}", f":root.nxm-p-{slug}-root"
    # the design's <body …>: its classes, CSS variables and data-* move to the
    # page wrapper (a nested page can't touch <body>); `xray` is a class the
    # design's JS toggles on body
    btag = re.search(r"<body([^>]*)>", html).group(1)
    battr = lambda n: (re.search(rf'{n}="([^"]*)"', btag) or [None, ""])[1]
    bclasses = battr("class").split()
    body_attrs = {"cls": " ".join(bclasses), "style": battr("style"),
                  "data": {k: v for k, v in re.findall(r'data-([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"', btag)}}
    hoisted, rules = scope_css(css, scope, rootcls, frozenset(bclasses) | {"xray"})
    extra = (f"\n{scope}{{{FONT_VARS}}}\n"
             f"{rootcls}{{--nav-h:68px;background:#060913}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta:only-child{{grid-column:1/-1}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nxm-navcta{{white-space:nowrap}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta{{height:48px;justify-content:center;font-size:1rem}}\n"
             f"@media (max-width:1080px){{{scope} .nv-act>.nxm-navcta{{display:none}}}}\n")
    css_out = ("/* GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py from the design package — do not edit. */\n"
               + "\n".join(hoisted) + "\n" + "\n".join(rules) + extra)

    # Markup: everything between <body> and the page script.
    js_at = rest.rfind("<script>")
    body, js = rest[:js_at], rest[js_at:]
    body = re.sub(r"^\s*<body[^>]*>", "", body.strip())
    body = relink(body)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):
        assert old in body, (slug, old); body = body.replace(old, new)

    body, nfoot = re.subn(r'<footer class="footer"[\s\S]*?</footer>', "", body)

    stray = balanced(body)

    wire = load_wire(slug)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "body"):

    # Script: the page's JS minus the Aurora runtime (mounted once by the layout).
    js = re.search(r"<script>([\s\S]*)</script>", js).group(1)
    assert AURORA_JS in js, "aurora.built.js not found verbatim"
    js = js.replace(AURORA_JS, "")
    js = js.replace("https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js", "/nxm/three.min.js")
    # body attributes now live on the page wrapper
    js = js.replace("document.body.dataset", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').dataset")
    js = js.replace("document.body.classList.toggle('xray'", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').classList.toggle('xray'")
    js = relink(js)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):

    js = js_buttons(js)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "js"):

    js = js.replace("'$' + Math.round(v).toLocaleString('en-US')", "__nxmMoney(Math.round(v), 0)")
    js = re.sub(r"'\$' \+ v\.toLocaleString\('en-US'(?:, \{[^}]*\})?\)", "__nxmMoney(v)", js)
    js = js.replace("'$' + v.toFixed(2)", "__nxmMoney(v)")
    assert "'$' +" not in js, f"{slug}: unconverted '$' + … money formatting in the page script"
    js = FX_PRELUDE + js

    STATUS[slug] = ("static (no system data)" if (wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False)) else "wired" if wire else "NOT WIRED") + (f", stale {stale}" if stale else "")

    open(f"{d}/page.css", "w").write(css_out)

        f"export const DESCRIPTION = {json.dumps(desc)};\n"
        f"export const BODY_HTML = {json.dumps(body)};\n"
        f"export const BODY_ATTRS = {json.dumps(body_attrs)};\n")
    open(f"{d}/script.ts", "w").write(

        f"export const PAGE_SCRIPT = {json.dumps(js)};\n")

    route = ROUTES[slug]
    loader = wire is not None and os.path.exists(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts")
    static = bool(wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False))
    assert wire is None or loader or static, f"{slug}: wire module without app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts"
    has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read()
    for r, fixed in routes_for(slug):
        if ("[" in r or fixed) and not has_meta:

            continue
        write_route(slug, r, fixed, loader)
    print(f"{slug:36} {BASE}{route if route != '/' else ''}  css {len(css_out)//1024}KB  body {len(body)//1024}KB  "

# ── routes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A page is a TEMPLATE when its route has [params] (e.g. /mods/[family]/[slug])
# or when tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json fans it out to many fixed routes
# (e.g. the game template -> /rust-server-hosting {family: "rust"}, ...).
# Loaders get the params: load(p) / meta(p).
def routes_for(slug):
    f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/routes/{slug}.json"
    if os.path.exists(f):
        return [(e["route"], e.get("params", {})) for e in json.load(open(f))]
    return [(ROUTES[slug], {})]

def js_buttons(js):
    """Buttons built by the design's scripts get the same hierarchy."""
    js = re.sub(r"class=\"btn \$\{([^}]*?)\s*\?\s*'btn-grad'\s*:\s*'btn-ghost'\}\"",
                lambda m: f'class="${{{m.group(1)} ? \'nxm-btn\' : \'nxm-glassbtn\'}}"', js)
    js = re.sub(r"class=\"au-btn \$\{([^}]*?)\s*\?\s*''\s*:\s*'au-btn--ghost'\}\"",
                lambda m: f'class="${{{m.group(1)} ? \'nxm-btn\' : \'nxm-ghost\'}}"', js)
    js, _ = swap_buttons(js)
    return js

**Rule: nothing mutates from the web tier.** Customer/admin actions (`lib/actions-dedicated-ops.ts`, `lib/actions-dedicated-ops-admin.ts`) only validate and insert a `DedicatedJob`. The worker sweep `dedicated-jobs` (`worker/dedicated-jobs.ts`, every 10 s) is the only place an upstream write happens: it runs `lib/dedicated/ops.ts` `runJobStep` and, for the real upstream, sends every write through `lib/ovh-admin/write.ts` `ovhAdminWrite` (rights check, per-actor and per-target rate limits, AuditLog before and after). Every job end also writes a `DedicatedServerEvent` and an AuditLog row; a failure notifies every ADMIN.

**Modes.**
- `dedicated_ovh_dry_run` (Setting, **default `"true"`**): nothing is sent; jobs finish "Dry run: ...". The admin server page shows a DRY RUN / LIVE badge. Set `"false"` to go live.
- `NXEON_DEDICATED_OVH_MOCK=1` (ignored when `NODE_ENV=production`): a fake upstream (`lib/dedicated/ovh-mock.ts`, file-backed so web + worker share it) for demos; the customer panel shows a "Demo machine" badge.

**Safety.** The target is always `DedicatedServer.providerServiceName` from OUR row (customers pass only our server id). A service name equal to any `Node.providerServerId` (or listed in Setting `dedicated_ovh_protected_services`) is refused before any call, so a mistyped link can never touch a platform node. rDNS / firewall IPs must lie inside the blocks upstream reports for that service. Disruptive actions (reboot, rescue, reinstall, handover): one at a time per server, 6 per hour per server; 30 actions per hour per customer; typed confirmation (the server's name) for reinstall; blocked while impersonating.

**What the customer can do** (`components/dedicated/DedicatedControlPanel.tsx`, on `/dashboard/dedicated/[id]` once the server is ACTIVE and linked):
- Overview: power, boot mode, network port and traffic, detected hardware (GETs, cached 20 s).
- Hard reboot (`POST /dedicated/server/{sn}/reboot`, task polled). No soft reboot exists upstream; the panel says to use `sudo reboot` for a graceful restart.
- Rescue: netboot rescue with the customer's SSH key (`PUT /dedicated/server/{sn}` `{bootId, rescueSshKey}` + reboot), back to disk the same way. If staff ever get a rescue password, they store it encrypted on the admin page (`rescueSecretEnc`) and the customer reveals it (`decryptSecret`).
- Reinstall: images from `GET .../install/compatibleTemplates`, filtered and renamed (`lib/dedicated/ops-core.ts` `offerableTemplates`: no Windows/licensed, panel, BYOI or "withapp" images), hostname + one of the customer's SSH keys, typed confirmation, `POST .../reinstall` `{operatingSystem, customizations:{hostname, sshKey}}`, progress from `.../install/status` + the task. Nxeon adds no deploy key (the VPS flow injects only the customer's keys too).
- Reverse DNS (`POST /ip/{block}/reverse`), network firewall per IPv4: on/off, add/remove rules (`/ip/{block}/firewall/...`, validated by the existing `lib/ovh-admin/validate.ts` rules).
- Extra IPv4 (1, 4 or 8): priced from `dedicated_ip_price_cents`, prorated to the next renewal (`extraIpProrateCents`), paid wallet-then-card (Stripe metadata `nxeonDedicatedIpOrder`, fulfil branch `dedicatedIpOrder`). Lands as `DedicatedIpOrder` PAID. **Nothing is bought until an ADMIN clicks "Approve purchase"** on the server page; approval enqueues `IP_ORDER`, which creates an upstream cart, adds the IP product for that size routed to the server (`destination`, `country`), checks out with the account's payment method, waits for delivery, then adds the block to the server and the monthly price to `renewalMonthlyCents` (+ `extraIpMonthlyCents`). "Reject & refund" returns the full charge to the wallet.
- Remote console: **not shipped to customers.** The upstream only offers its own hosted KVM/SOL pages (`/features/ipmi/access`), so the panel offers "Open a ticket" and staff open the console.

**Handover (auto-install).** On a PENDING/PROVISIONING server, after staff buy the machine and save its service name, "Install & hand over" (admin server page) enqueues `HANDOVER`: install the OS the customer ordered (matched by label) with the customer's first SSH key, then mark ACTIVE, fill IPs from upstream, set hostname/OS, notify in-app and send the `dedicated_server_ready` email template (`prisma/seed-email-templates.ts`; never sent in mock mode). A customer with no SSH key: the button refuses; deliver credentials by hand.

content.thinking:
The 178px height suggests a competing rule is winning despite my !important. This could be a cascade layers issue—if the nxm/aurora CSS sets height:auto with !important inside a @layer, that would actually override my unlayered !important declaration, since important rules inside layers take precedence over important rules outside layers.

The fix is to apply inline style with !important directly on the img elements in the markup, since inline author-origin !important beats all stylesheet importants. I'll add this to the logos in the loader plate, JS card, and chip markup.

input.message:
## Dedicated servers: private preview, checkout, automated actions, bare-metal marketing page

The full customer flow works end to end on my own instance for the preview account only, including a real Stripe **test-mode** card payment. No live charge and no upstream write against real servers were made. Automated actions ship in dry-run by default, so nothing is sent to real machines until the owner turns it on.

**Branch:** `feature/dedicated-private-preview` in worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-dedicated2`, cut from `main` with `feature/dedicated-servers` merged in.
- `accde1bdd7`: the merge. Two conflicts, both resolved by keeping both sides: the worker sweep list and the docs.
- `3e640a0b6d`: preview gate and the online checkout.
- `79e05b0b5a`: automated server actions (Phase 2), the marketing page and nav, the CPU/GPU logos.

Nothing was deployed or merged to `main`, no services were restarted, `/opt/nxeon` was not touched, and no customer was contacted.

### Preview gate
Only `nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com` can see any of it until the owner sets `dedicated_public_enabled=true`. Launch needs no code change.

What it covers:
- `/dedicated-servers`, both the new marketing-site version and the old one.
- `/dashboard/dedicated`, the order catalogue, the configure page and the server page.
- Every customer server action (requests, credentials, checkout, automated actions, extra IPs).
- The portal sidebar entry, the marketing nav tab, the Products-menu entry, the mobile-menu link, and the "Need more power?" strips on the VPS and pricing pages.

Everyone else:
- Signed-in customers get `notFound()`. One caveat: under `/dashboard`, Next serves the 404 page with HTTP 200 because the existing `app/dashboard/loading.tsx` starts streaming first. This is the same as any other dashboard 404 in this app.
- Signed-out visitors are sent to login, the same as for any `/dashboard` URL.
- Pages are noindex and stay out of the sitemap until public.
- Admin pages are unchanged and stay admin-only.

**`lib/preview-access.ts`** — identical copy for the mod builder branch:
```ts
/**
 * PRIVATE PREVIEW GATE — one tiny helper shared by every unreleased customer
 * feature ("dedicated", "modbuilder"). Keep this file IDENTICAL on every branch
 * that carries it: it has no feature-specific imports.
 *
 * Who is allowed: the accounts whose email is in the allowlist for that feature.
 *   1. Setting `preview_access_emails_<feature>` (comma-separated), if that row exists;
 *   2. else Setting `preview_access_emails` (shared by every feature), if that row exists;
 *   3. else DEFAULT_PREVIEW_EMAILS below (the owner's own customer account).
 * An empty Setting value means "nobody". Matching is case-insensitive on the
 * account's email. A DB error fails CLOSED (nobody is a preview user).
 *
 * Callers decide what "not allowed" looks like (normally `notFound()`, so the
 * feature is indistinguishable from a route that does not exist).
 */
import { getSetting } from "./settings";

export const PREVIEW_FEATURES = ["dedicated", "modbuilder"] as const;
export type PreviewFeature = (typeof PREVIEW_FEATURES)[number];

export const PREVIEW_ACCESS_SETTING = "preview_access_emails";
export const DEFAULT_PREVIEW_EMAILS = ["nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com"];

/** Sentinel: getSetting returns it only when no Setting row exists. */
const UNSET = "\u0000unset";

export function parsePreviewEmails(raw: string | null | undefined): string[] {
  return (raw ?? "")
    .split(/[,\s;]+/)
    .map((e) => e.trim().toLowerCase())
    .filter((e) => e.includes("@"));
}

/** Pure decision (unit-tested). */
export function emailInPreviewList(email: string | null | undefined, list: readonly string[]): boolean {
  const e = (email ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
  return !!e && list.some((x) => x.trim().toLowerCase() === e);
}

export async function previewAllowlist(feature: PreviewFeature): Promise<string[]> {
  if (!(PREVIEW_FEATURES as readonly string[]).includes(feature)) return [];
  const own = await getSetting(`${PREVIEW_ACCESS_SETTING}_${feature}`, UNSET);
  if (own !== UNSET) return parsePreviewEmails(own);
  const shared = await getSetting(PREVIEW_ACCESS_SETTING, UNSET);
  if (shared !== UNSET) return parsePreviewEmails(shared);
  return [...DEFAULT_PREVIEW_EMAILS];
}

/** True only for a signed-in account on the feature's allowlist. Never throws. */
export async function isPreviewUser(
  user: { email?: string | null } | null | undefined,
  feature: PreviewFeature,
): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!user?.email) return false;
  try {
    return emailInPreviewList(user.email, await previewAllowlist(feature));
  } catch {
    return false; // fail CLOSED
  }
}
```
The dedicated gate itself is `lib/dedicated/gate.ts`: access is granted when the public flag is on or the account is a preview user.

### Customer flow, step by step
1. **Browse** (`/dashboard/dedicated/order`): only in-stock builds are shown.
   - Filters: location (all regions listed, sold-out ones labelled), AMD / Intel / GPU (with logos), cores, memory, storage and price.
   - Prices are the pricing-rules price including markup. Every build says "Online within 24 hours". Empty, no-match and loading states are designed.
2. **Configure** (`/dashboard/dedicated/order/[id]`): location, memory, storage, network, OS, monthly or annual term, and a server name.
   - Memory/storage combinations that are out of stock are disabled.
   - Annual is 12 × the monthly price, because the pricing rules define no annual discount.
3. **Review:** the server re-prices the order and shows specs, setup, tax, total today, the renewal as charged ("$X/yr" for annual) and a wallet toggle.
4. **Pay:** the portal's existing wallet-then-card path. If the wallet covers it, the order is placed immediately. Otherwise the remainder goes through the inline card form, and fulfilment charges exactly the price stamped before payment. One order key per checkout means a double click or retry places at most one order.
5. **Order lands** as a `DedicatedServer` in **PENDING**, with a paid invoice. Admins get a notification and a build sheet on `/admin/dedicated/servers/[id]`.
6. **Server page:** status timeline, specs, IPs once assigned, login, renewal, invoices and support. Fully automated controls appear once the server is delivered.

### Phase 2: automated actions on a delivered server
The web tier only creates jobs. The new worker sweep in `worker/dedicated-jobs.ts` is the only place a write to the upstream API happens, through the existing audited `ovhAdminWrite` wrapper.
- **Safety:** customers pass only our server id; the upstream service name comes from our own row. Any service name belonging to a platform node is refused before any call. Actions are rate-limited, one restart/rescue/reinstall at a time per server, reinstall needs the server name typed to confirm, and actions are blocked while impersonating.
- **Hard reboot.** There is no soft reboot in the upstream API, so the panel tells customers to run `sudo reboot` inside the OS for a graceful restart.
- **Rescue mode** uses the customer's own SSH key. Back-to-disk works the same way. If staff ever receive a rescue password, they can store it encrypted on the admin page and the customer can reveal it.
- **OS reinstall:** compatible images with customer-facing names (no Windows, panel or bring-your-own images), hostname, one of the customer's SSH keys, and a progress bar until done. No Nxeon key is added; the VPS flow doesn't add one either.
- **Reverse DNS and a per-IP network firewall** (on/off, add/remove rules), reusing the existing OVH controls' validation.
- **Hardware, status and bandwidth view.**
- **Extra IPv4** (1, 4 or 8 addresses): prorated to renewal and paid wallet-then-card. Nothing is bought upstream until an admin clicks **Approve purchase**. The worker then orders the IPs, attaches them, and adds the monthly price to the renewal. **Reject** refunds the full charge to the wallet.
- **Handover:** after the admin saves the service name on a pending order, **Install & hand over** installs the ordered OS with the customer's SSH key, marks the server ACTIVE, fills in the IPs and notifies the customer. The email goes through the template system (new `dedicated_server_ready` template) and is never sent in mock mode.
- **Remote console is not shipped to customers.** The upstream only offers its own hosted console page, so customers get "Open a ticket" instead.

### Marketing, nav and logos
- **New page** `/dedicated-servers`, built as a native page on the new marketing site and generated by the porter's own script ("wired", no stale prices).
  - Hero uses the owner's rack art, with a live in-stock "spec plate" and real stats.
  - Live filterable catalogue: region, AMD / Intel / NVIDIA logos, cores, RAM, storage, price.
  - Sections: what's included, how it works, bare metal vs VPS, live locations, FAQ.
  - "Configure" goes straight into the portal configurator; signed-out visitors go through `/register?next=…`.
  - Copy says "bare metal", makes no SLA claims, never names the supplier, and shows no invented stats.
- **Nav and upsell links** are injected at render time only for allowed viewers.
- **Logos:** AMD, Intel and NVIDIA are detected from the CPU/GPU model and use the existing SVGs. On the portal's light theme they are inverted with the hue restored.
- Locations in the same metro now have distinct customer names: France (North 1/2), France (Paris A/B/C).

### What was verified, and how
- **Throwaway database:** a separate Postgres on port 55447 (`/tank/pg-dedprev`, now stopped), loaded with a real read-only catalogue sync of 240 plans.
- **Real Stripe test-mode payment:** test keys from staging, test card 4242, through the inline card form. The order landed PENDING and the ledger was exact: wallet $50 + card $1,791.98 − total $1,841.98 (annual term + $42.10 setup) leaves $0. One invoice, and no duplicate top-up invoice.
- **Wallet-only payment** also verified end to end.
- **Tests:**
  - New: `preview-access`, `dedicated-order`, `dedicated-ops` (every upstream write path, checked call by call against the fake upstream).
  - Updated: `dedicated-gate`, `dedicated-brand-voice`.
  - Opt-in DB test (`dedicated-order-db`): gate overrides, displayed price equals charged price, card and wallet placement each happen once, tampered prices are refused, and a worker tick runs end to end including the dry-run and protected-node refusals. All 8 pass.

### Preview gate
Only `nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com` can see any of it until the owner sets `dedicated_public_enabled=true`. Launch needs no code change.

What it covers:
- `/dedicated-servers`, both the new marketing-site version and the old one.
- `/dashboard/dedicated`, the order catalogue, the configure page and the server page.
- Every customer server action (requests, credentials, checkout, automated actions, extra IPs).
- The portal sidebar entry, the marketing nav tab, the Products-menu entry, the mobile-menu link, and the "Need more power?" strips on the VPS and pricing pages.

Everyone else:
- Signed-in customers get `notFound()`. One caveat: under `/dashboard`, Next serves the 404 page with HTTP 200 because the existing `app/dashboard/loading.tsx` starts streaming first. This is the same as any other dashboard 404 in this app.

**`lib/preview-access.ts`** — identical copy for the mod builder branch:
```ts
/**
 * PRIVATE PREVIEW GATE — one tiny helper shared by every unreleased customer
 * feature ("dedicated", "modbuilder"). Keep this file IDENTICAL on every branch
 * that carries it: it has no feature-specific imports.
 *
 * Who is allowed: the accounts whose email is in the allowlist for that feature.
 *   1. Setting `preview_access_emails_<feature>` (comma-separated), if that row exists;
 *   2. else Setting `preview_access_emails` (shared by every feature), if that row exists;
 *   3. else DEFAULT_PREVIEW_EMAILS below (the owner's own customer account).
 * An empty Setting value means "nobody". Matching is case-insensitive on the
 * account's email. A DB error fails CLOSED (nobody is a preview user).
 *
 * Callers decide what "not allowed" looks like (normally `notFound()`, so the
 * feature is indistinguishable from a route that does not exist).
 */
import { getSetting } from "./settings";

export const PREVIEW_FEATURES = ["dedicated", "modbuilder"] as const;
export type PreviewFeature = (typeof PREVIEW_FEATURES)[number];

export const PREVIEW_ACCESS_SETTING = "preview_access_emails";
export const DEFAULT_PREVIEW_EMAILS = ["nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com"];

/** Sentinel: getSetting returns it only when no Setting row exists. */
const UNSET = "\u0000unset";

export function parsePreviewEmails(raw: string | null | undefined): string[] {
  return (raw ?? "")
    .split(/[,\s;]+/)
    .map((e) => e.trim().toLowerCase())
    .filter((e) => e.includes("@"));
}

/** Pure decision (unit-tested). */
export function emailInPreviewList(email: string | null | undefined, list: readonly string[]): boolean {
  const e = (email ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
  return !!e && list.some((x) => x.trim().toLowerCase() === e);
}

export async function previewAllowlist(feature: PreviewFeature): Promise<string[]> {
  if (!(PREVIEW_FEATURES as readonly string[]).includes(feature)) return [];
  const own = await getSetting(`${PREVIEW_ACCESS_SETTING}_${feature}`, UNSET);
  if (own !== UNSET) return parsePreviewEmails(own);
  const shared = await getSetting(PREVIEW_ACCESS_SETTING, UNSET);
  if (shared !== UNSET) return parsePreviewEmails(shared);
  return [...DEFAULT_PREVIEW_EMAILS];
}

/** True only for a signed-in account on the feature's allowlist. Never throws. */
export async function isPreviewUser(
  user: { email?: string | null } | null | undefined,
  feature: PreviewFeature,
): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!user?.email) return false;
  try {
    return emailInPreviewList(user.email, await previewAllowlist(feature));
  } catch {
    return false; // fail CLOSED
  }
}
```
The dedicated gate itself is `lib/dedicated/gate.ts`: access is granted when the public flag is on or the account is a preview user.

### Customer flow, step by step
1. **Browse** (`/dashboard/dedicated/order`): only in-stock builds are shown.
   - Filters: location (all regions listed, sold-out ones labelled), AMD / Intel / GPU (with logos), cores, memory, storage and price.
   - Prices are the pricing-rules price including markup. Every build says "Online within 24 hours". Empty, no-match and loading states are designed.
2. **Configure** (`/dashboard/dedicated/order/[id]`): location, memory, storage, network, OS, monthly or annual term, and a server name.
   - Memory/storage combinations that are out of stock are disabled.
   - Annual is 12 × the monthly price, because the pricing rules define no annual discount.
3. **Review:** the server re-prices the order and shows specs, setup, tax, total today, the renewal as charged ("$X/yr" for annual) and a wallet toggle.
4. **Pay:** the portal's existing wallet-then-card path. If the wallet covers it, the order is placed immediately. Otherwise the remainder goes through the inline card form, and fulfilment charges exactly the price stamped before payment. One order key per checkout means a double click or retry places at most one order.
5. **Order lands** as a `DedicatedServer` in **PENDING**, with a paid invoice. Admins get a notification and a build sheet on `/admin/dedicated/servers/[id]`.
6. **Server page:** status timeline, specs, IPs once assigned, login, renewal, invoices and support. Fully automated controls appear once the server is delivered.

### Phase 2: automated actions on a delivered server
The web tier only creates jobs. The new worker sweep in `worker/dedicated-jobs.ts` is the only place a write to the upstream API happens, through the existing audited `ovhAdminWrite` wrapper.
- **Safety:** customers pass only our server id; the upstream service name comes from our own row. Any service name belonging to a platform node is refused before any call. Actions are rate-limited, one restart/rescue/reinstall at a time per server, reinstall needs the server name typed to confirm, and actions are blocked while impersonating.
- **Hard reboot.** There is no soft reboot in the upstream API, so the panel tells customers to run `sudo reboot` inside the OS for a graceful restart.
- **Rescue mode** uses the customer's own SSH key. Back-to-disk works the same way. If staff ever receive a rescue password, they can store it encrypted on the admin page and the customer can reveal it.
- **OS reinstall:** compatible images with customer-facing names (no Windows, panel or bring-your-own images), hostname, one of the customer's SSH keys, and a progress bar until done. No Nxeon key is added; the VPS flow doesn't add one either.
- **Reverse DNS and a per-IP network firewall** (on/off, add/remove rules), reusing the existing OVH controls' validation.
- **Hardware, status and bandwidth view.**
- **Extra IPv4** (1, 4 or 8 addresses): prorated to renewal and paid wallet-then-card. Nothing is bought upstream until an admin clicks **Approve purchase**. The worker then orders the IPs, attaches them, and adds the monthly price to the renewal. **Reject** refunds the full charge to the wallet.
- **Handover:** after the admin saves the service name on a pending order, **Install & hand over** installs the ordered OS with the customer's SSH key, marks the server ACTIVE, fills in the IPs and notifies the customer. The email goes through the template system (new `dedicated_server_ready` template) and is never sent in mock mode.
- **Remote console is not shipped to customers.** The upstream only offers its own hosted console page, so customers get "Open a ticket" instead.
